text: Qadam — your next worthwhile stop in Astana. A recorded live UI demonstration of a walking assistant for residents and first-time visitors.
Start with an idea, a starting point and the time you have. Suggestions appear beside the map.
Scenario 1: a 60-minute walk near Mega Silk Way. Choose Walk and set the starting point.
Qadam first retrieves saved places and checks distance, available time and selected constraints.
OpenAI receives a small set of retrieved evidence. The application validates its selection against those candidates.
Each suggestion includes a reason, an activity idea and approximate travel and visit time.
Select a suggestion or its numbered map pin to calculate a pedestrian route.
Route time is shown separately from the initial planning estimate. Entrances and current conditions remain unverified.
Scenario 2: a first visit near Bayterek, with 90 minutes available.
Change the starting point and choose Discover. Qadam searches the saved dataset for suitable nearby options.
Recommendations are alternatives. Compare their activities and estimated time before selecting a stop.
Source facts and generated activity ideas are distinguished. Missing details are not invented.
Scenario 3: a coffee break near Bayterek, with 45 minutes available.
Type a simple request or use the coffee shortcut. Supported categories and simple durations are interpreted locally.
Selected filters shape retrieval. Live AI selects grounded suggestions from the eligible candidates.
Choose a coffee suggestion to see its walking route and updated total time.
The full dataset stays local. Selected evidence is sent to OpenAI; rounded endpoints are sent to the routing provider.
Qadam helps you decide where to go next. This prototype covers three walking scenarios, with limited data coverage and clearly labeled uncertainty.
